candidates.statement: 1,1,2-TRICHLOROETHENE 2 Genotoxicity 3 Generally negative results when pure, unstabilised trichloroethylene is used. 4 Trichloroethylene is often stabilised with 1,2-epoxybutane or epichlorohydrin, both of which 5 are known mutagens and are probably responsible for the positive results seen in some 6 studies. Refs. McGregor DB et al., Environ. Mol. Mutagen. 1989 13 197-202 7 Shimada T et al., Cell Biol. Toxicol. 1985 1 (3) 159-79 8 Ashby J. In Progress in Mut. Res. 1981 1 111-71. 9 Trichloroethylene should not be considered genotoxic. 10 Carcinogenicity 11 Rats Osborne-Mendel rats given 500 or 1000 mg/kg/day 5 days/week by gavage for 18 12 months did not develop tumours. NEL 1000 mg/kg. 13 Ref. NCI Tech Report No. 2 NIH Pub. No. 76-802 (1976) 14
